教習所の申し込みから、学科・構内・路上の試験、免許を取ったあとの初めての運転、給: From signing up at a driving school and taking the theory, course and road tests to your first drive with a license, filling up and traffic violations. Conversations for getting your license in China and hitting the road.
教習所に申し込む: Signing up at a driving school
蘇州の日系メーカーで働いて二年目の小林さん。東京育ちで免許を持っていないが、週末: Misaki Kobayashi is in her second year at a Japanese manufacturer in Suzhou. She grew up in Tokyo and never got a license, but she'd love to drive herself to factories and lakes in the suburbs on weekends, so she has decided to take the plunge and get a license in China. On Saturday morning she visits the front desk of a driving school near her office.
教習所の受付スタッフ、三十代。てきぱきしていて説明がうまい: Front desk staff at the driving school, in her thirties. Efficient and good at explaining
蘇州の日系メーカーで働く日本人会社員、二十六歳。東京育ちで車の免許は持っていない: A Japanese office worker at a Japanese manufacturer in Suzhou, 26. Grew up in Tokyo and has no driver's license
受付スタッフとお客さん。窓口での相談なので、スタッフは丁寧ながらも親しみのある話: Staff member and customer. Since this is a consultation at the counter, the staff member is polite but friendly. At a Chinese driving school's front desk it's fine to ask directly about fees and how long it takes to pass. If you don't understand a word, ask right then and there.
こんにちは、教習のお申し込みですか。: Hello, are you here to sign up for driving lessons?
「学车」は「車の運転を習う」こと。教習所に通うことを中国語ではこのひと言で言いま: 「学车」 means "to learn to drive." In Chinese this one word covers going to driving school. 「报名」 means "to sign up, to register," and is used widely, for exams, classes and more.
はい。私は日本人なんですが、外国人もここで習えますか。: Yes. I'm Japanese. Can foreigners learn here too?
大丈夫ですよ。日本の免許はお持ちですか。お持ちなら、科目一の試験を受けるだけで済: Yes, that's fine. Do you have a Japanese license? If you do, you only need to take the Subject 1 test.
中国の運転免許の試験は、一般に「科目一」から「科目四」と呼ばれます。外国の有効な: China's driving tests are generally called 「科目一」 (Subject 1) through 「科目四」 (Subject 4). People who hold a valid foreign license can, if they meet the requirements, get a Chinese license just by passing Subject 1, the theory test. If you already have a license from home, check this route first.
免許は持っていないんです。東京にいたころはずっと電車だったので。: I don't have a license. When I lived in Tokyo I always took the train.
それなら最初から習うことになりますね。マニュアル車とオートマ車、どちらにしますか: Then you'll be starting from scratch. Would you like to learn manual or automatic?
「手动挡」はマニュアル車、「自动挡」はオートマ車。「挡」はギアのことです。免許の: 「手动挡」 is a manual car and 「自动挡」 is an automatic. 「挡」 means gear. In terms of license types, manual is 「C1」 and automatic-only is 「C2」, and people say 「考C1」 or 「考C2」 in conversation too.
C1はマニュアルで、取ればマニュアル車もオートマ車も運転できます。C2はオートマ: C1 is manual. Once you have it, you can drive both manual and automatic cars. C2 only lets you drive automatics, but it's a bit easier to learn.
せっかくなのでしっかり習いたいです。じゃあC1にします。教習料は全部でいくらです: Since I'm doing this, I want to learn properly. I'll go with C1. How much are the fees in total?
「报C1」の「报」は「报名」の略で、「C1に申し込む」。料金を聞くときは「一共多: The 「报」 in 「报C1」 is short for 「报名」, so it means "sign up for C1." When asking about fees, confirm the total with 「一共多少钱」 so you won't be surprised by extra charges later.
全部で五千八百元です。教習料と試験料が含まれています。再受験の場合は別に料金がか: 5,800 yuan in total. That includes the lesson fees and the test fees. Retaking a test costs extra.
「五千八」は「五千八百」のこと。金額では最後の単位を省くのが普通です。「补考」は: 「五千八」 means 5,800. With amounts of money, the last unit is usually dropped. 「补考」 means "retake." Checking up front what it costs if you fail is the key to choosing a driving school.
わかりました。申し込みには何が必要ですか。: Got it. What do I need to bring to sign up?
パスポート、居留許可、それに健康診断の証明です。健康診断は指定の病院で受けられて: Your passport, residence permit and a medical certificate. You can get the medical check at a designated hospital, and it takes half a day.
外国人が中国で免許を取るには、パスポートと居留許可が必要です。「体检」は健康診断: To get a license in China, foreigners need a passport and a residence permit. 「体检」 is a medical checkup, which tests things like eyesight and color vision. Requirements can vary by region, so check before you sign up.
だいたいどれくらいで免許が取れますか。: About how long does it take to get a license?
練習する時間次第ですね。週末だけ通うなら、だいたい三、四か月でしょうか。: It depends on how much time you practice. If you only come on weekends, about three or four months, I'd say.
「看＋名詞」で「～次第だ」。「看情况」（状況次第）、「看天气」（天気次第）のよう: 「看」 + noun means "it depends on...." Like 「看情况」 (depends on the situation) and 「看天气」 (depends on the weather), it's a handy lead-in when you can't give a definite answer.
わかりました。じゃあ、今日申し込みます。: Okay. Then I'll sign up today.
かしこまりました。まずこちらの用紙にご記入ください。: Certainly. Please fill in this form first.

必要な条件が一つだけで十分だと伝える言い方。手続きの説明でよく使われ、聞く側も「: A way of saying that a single condition is enough. It's often used when explaining procedures, and it reassures the listener ("That's all?"). You can drop 「只要」 and just say 「……就行了」 to mean "that'll do."
お持ちなら科目一を受けるだけでいいです。: If you have one, you only need to take Subject 1.
パスポートを持ってくるだけで大丈夫です。: All you need to bring is your passport.
毎日一時間練習しさえすればいいですよ。: As long as you practice for an hour every day, you'll be fine.
二つのうちどちらかを選んでもらう疑問文。「还是」を使った疑問文には、文末に「吗」: A question asking someone to choose between two options. Questions with 「还是」 don't take 「吗」 at the end. At a driving school there are lots of choices to make: the type of car, time slots, locations and so on.
マニュアルとオートマ、どちらを習いたいですか。: Would you like to learn manual or automatic?
土曜に来る？ それとも日曜？: Are you coming on Saturday or Sunday?
結果が何によって決まるかを表す口語表現。「看情况」「看天气」のように短く言えるの: A colloquial way of saying what an outcome depends on. Because it can be short, like 「看情况」 or 「看天气」, it's a handy answer when you can't promise anything. If you say 「看你」 to someone, it means "it's up to you."
練習する時間次第です。: It depends on how much time you practice.
行くかどうかは天気次第だね。: Whether we go or not depends on the weather.
教習所、語学学校、ジムなど、料金やコースを相談して申し込む場面に。種類の違い、総: For signing up after asking about fees and courses: at a driving school, language school, gym and so on. Ask about five things (the differences between options, the total, extra fees, what to bring and how long it takes) and you'll rarely run into trouble later.
総額だけ聞いて申し込み、再受験料や追加の練習料金を確かめないのは危険です。また「: Signing up after hearing only the total, without checking retake fees or extra practice fees, is risky. Also, rather than saying 「我不懂」 and going quiet, asking straight out about the word you don't know, like 「C1是什么？」, gets the conversation much further.
周さんは、外国人の申し込みに少し驚きつつも歓迎しています。小林さんが「多学一点儿: Zhou Fang is a little surprised to have a foreigner signing up, but she welcomes it. She likes that Misaki chose C1 to 「多学一点儿」, thinks she seems conscientious, and intends to guide her carefully through the paperwork.
中国では大学生のうちに免許を取る人が多く、夏休みや冬休みの教習所は学生でいっぱい: In China many people get their license while at university, and driving schools fill up with students over the summer and winter breaks. Driving schools are called 「驾校」, and the usual style is to practice the test tasks over and over with an assigned instructor. Fees vary widely by region and school, and some offer courses like a 「VIP班」, where you practice one-on-one with an instructor at times you choose. Asking for reviews and recommendations from people you know before signing up is the Chinese way.

マニュアル車を習いたい: I want to learn to drive a manual car

試験料は後払いでいい: You can pay the test fee later
不合格なら返金される: You get a refund if you fail

料金の総額を聞くときの自然な言い方は？: What's a natural way to ask for the total price?
「一共多少钱？」で「全部でいくらですか」。語順は「一共」が先です。: 「一共多少钱？」 means "How much is it in total?" 「一共」 comes first.

練習する時間次第です: It depends on how much time you practice
「看＋名詞」は「～次第だ」という意味。期間がどれくらいかかるかは練習の時間によっ: 「看」 + noun means "it depends on...." She's answering that how long it takes depends on how much time is spent practicing.
